coverage: WTMC2021 entity-level convergence and sensitivity analysis
RF / IF / KDIS cross-method baseline stability
Post-review structural ablation of SBV and SREP constituent threshold conditions
architecture_note: The original Python notebook handles analytical logic including thresholding, convergence, and RCI, while the Cypher layer handles graph construction and raw centrality export. Threshold application is performed in Python on values exported from Neo4j, preserving graph-database portability. The later windowed-flow experiments use source-hour structural and behavioral operators under a frozen-policy design in which operator definitions, feature identities, window duration, percentile policies, and fusion rules are fixed before external evaluation, while numeric threshold values are estimated from the declared calibration population of each environment.

post_review_ablation.purpose: Evaluate whether the conjunctive structure of the frozen structural operators provides measurable value beyond their individual threshold components without redesigning or retuning the original frozen-policy operators.
post_review_ablation.methodological_note: The ablation was performed after completion of the original frozen-policy external evaluation. It was not used to redesign, retune, or redefine S_BV, S_REP, S_T, the one-hour windowing policy, percentile policies, behavioral mechanisms, or fusion rules.
main_findings: The SBV conjunction substantially improved selectivity relative to its individual rate-only and count-only components.
In Improved CSE-CIC-IDS2018, SBV reduced false positives from 8389 under RATE_ONLY_P99 to 148 while retaining the same 50 true positives.
The SREP P50 flow-count guard provided no additional selectivity in Improved CSE-CIC-IDS2018 because REP_ONLY_P99 and S_REP produced identical results.
In WTMC2021, the SREP P50 flow-count guard removed two true-positive windows without removing any false positives.
The original SREP definition remains unchanged to preserve the integrity of the frozen-policy experiment.

reproducibility_note: The November 2026 runtime snapshots document the environments used for the post-review reproducibility reruns and structural ablation analyses. They do not retrospectively redefine the May 2026 software environment of the original locked KDIS/HGBF protocol.
limitations: Dataset files are not included in the repository.
The original locked notebook contains Google Drive mounting and local path assumptions.
Neo4j GDS queries are optional and environment-dependent.
Dependency versions under original_protocol correspond to the May 2026 Colab snapshot used for the original protocol.
The post-review ablation reruns were executed under later November 2026 Colab environments whose complete package states are preserved in reproducibility/environments/.
The two November 2026 Colab runtimes were not identical; notably, WTMC2021 used NumPy 2.4.6 whereas the Improved CSE-CIC-IDS2018 rerun used NumPy 2.1.3.
The structural ablation is diagnostic and post-hoc and must not be interpreted as retrospective optimization of the frozen-policy detector.
